notes.decision: The triple-ⲣⲥ̄ formation in lines 25-27 functions as ornamental chapter-heading framework with the Coptic numeral ⲣⲥ̄ (= 100) as decorative dividers around the title text. Translated each ⲣⲥ̄ literally as '·100·' to preserve the decorative function. The chapter number (100) does not correspond to the actual Kephalaia numbering at this page (which is in the higher chapters), so the ⲣⲥ̄ may be ornamental section-marker rather than literal chapter number.

notes.coptic_form: ⲙⲛ̄ ⲣⲁⲱⲉ ⲉⲱⲁϩⲙⲟⲩⲛ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲃⲁⲗ ⲍⲙ̄ ⲡⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ⲩⲁⲃⲁⲗ
notes.decision: Translated 'There is no joy that abides nor any sight in the world forever.' ⲙⲛ̄ as existential negation; ⲣⲁⲱⲉ = ⲣⲁϣⲉ 'joy'; ⲉⲱⲁϩⲙⲟⲩⲛ = ⲉ-ϣⲁϥ-ⲙⲟⲩⲛ 'which keeps lasting/abiding'; ⲙⲛ̄ ⲃⲁⲗ probably 'and (no) eye/sight' as a parallel negation; ⲩⲁⲃⲁⲗ = ϣⲁ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forever.' The chapter-heading sets up the next kephalaion's argument that nothing in the world stands forever, even sun and moon are subject to change.

Translated 'they neither cast a shadow nor know.' ⲑⲁⲓⲃⲉ = ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' verbalized — 'they overshadow / cast shadow.' Negative ⲉⲛ following each verb is the Lyc. circumstantial negative. The double negation continues a series describing what the sun and moon do or fail to do as cosmic luminaries (i.e., they are not autonomous masters but are themselves under summons — line 33).

Translated 'set near' tentatively. The form is obscure: possibly Lyc qualitative of ϩⲱⲛ 'approach, draw near,' or an emphatic particle akin to ϩⲱⲱϥ. In context with ϩⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ 'he stands fast,' a sense of 'being set/positioned' fits. Confidence low.

Translated 'king-face' (face of a king). Standard Coptic compound: ϩⲟ 'face' + ⲛ̄- (genitive) + ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'king.' The enemy presents himself as a kingly visage in places that do not befit him — central image of this section.

Translated 'she is drawn taut' tentatively. Likely Lyc qualitative on ⲭⲱⲗⲕ̄/ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'draw, set in array, bind' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲭⲱⲗⲕ̄/ⲭⲱⲗⲍ 'to draw, draw up'). The 3sg.f prefix ⲥ- gives 'she is drawn (bound/taut).' Pairs naturally with following ⲥⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲟ̄ 'she stands fast.'

Translated 'abusing' tentatively. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲑⲛⲟ/ⲑⲃⲃⲓⲟ 'humble, bring low' (cf. accumulated ⲑⲃⲓⲟ 'humble'), or a related verb of mistreatment. Listed in a sequence of harms inflicted on the soul (afflict/abuse/tear/eat).
Translated 'tearing' tentatively. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲡⲱϫⲝ/ⲡⲱⲕⲥ 'tear apart, rend.' Fits the catalogue of violence done to the soul. Confidence low; flag for parallels.

Translated 'the thorn.' Lyc reflex of ⲥⲟⲣⲧⲉ 'thorn, thistle' (Crum). Pairs antithetically with ⲡϣⲏⲛ 'the tree' as the locus where the soul is bound — recalling the Manichaean motif of the soul caught both in the beautiful tree and the bitter thorn.
Translated 'his heart at rest.' ϩⲙⲁⲧⲛⲉ likely a Lyc compound on ⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ/ⲙ̄ⲧⲟⲛ 'rest' with prefix. The enemy's complacent rest in stolen wealth that does not befit him.
Translated 'claws.' Lyc form of ⲧⲃⲓⲝ/ⲧⲃⲏⲓϫ 'claw, talon' (Sah). The phrase 'from under the claws of the enemy' is a Manichaean idiom for the soul's captive state.

Translated 'release her forth.' Treating ⲃⲱⲧⲉ as Lyc orthographic variant of ⲃⲱⲗ 'release, dissolve' (cf. accumulated ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release' as soteriological terminology). The holy ones release the soul from death. Soteriological-redemptive register.
Translated 'the bond.' Lyc form of ⲙⲣ̄ⲣⲉ/ⲙⲣⲡⲉ 'bond, fetter' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲙⲣⲡⲉ 'bond/fetter'). The eschatological binding of the enemy in fetters at the end of time.

Translated 'they shall not give ear to grief any more.' Reading ⲥⲱⲧ as a Lyc form/reduction of ⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'hear, give ear' — the construction ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ ⲁ- 'listen to' fits both syntax and sense. Alternative readings ('not return to grief,' 'not pursue grief') are possible. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'they shall be in their condition.' ⲣ̄ + ⲧⲟⲩϩⲉ = 'do/be in their manner.' ⲧⲟⲩϩⲉ = ⲧⲉⲩ-ϩⲉ 'their way, their manner.' The doubling 'their condition, their condition again, the manner...' emphasizes the restoration of the souls to their primordial state.
Translated 'gaze upon.' Lyc reflex of ⲓⲱⲣⲙⲉ 'gaze, look' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲓⲱⲣⲙⲉ 'to gaze'). The eyes that gaze upon the enemy's foul forms — first reason for the holy ones' incomplete joy.

Coptic numeral ⲣ=100, ⲍ=7, giving 107. The chapter is bracketed by ⲣⲍ ⲣⲍ marks, a standard Kephalaia layout convention. The intervening damaged dotted line likely held additional decorative material now lost.
